Each version reflected a different stage in Guild's OEM partnerships, beginning with a rebranded Mosrite Fuzzrite and later evolving through Electro-Harmonix designs that paralleled the Axis Fuzz and early Big Muff circuits. All versions were built in folded heavy gauge steel enclosures and powered by a 9V battery. v1: Mosrite version The first version of the Guild Foxey Lady was built by Mosrite in 1968, using the same silicon transistor circuit as the Mosrite Fuzzrite designed by Ed Sanner. Guild president Al Dronge already had a history with Semie Moseley, dating back to their earlier collaboration on the Vibromute vibrato project in 1963, and the two remained in contact afterward. When fuzz pedals became commercially successful, Dronge commissioned Moseley to produce a Guild branded version of the Fuzzrite.
